q: 1. In hydrometer analysis the principle used is .............
explain: Stoke's Law relates the settling velocity of fine particles in suspension to their size, forming the basis of hydrometer analysis.

q: 2. The drop of the cup for the liquid limit determination is .............
explain: In the Casagrande liquid limit device, the standard drop height of the cup is 10 mm.

q: 3. Clay can be classified as
explain: Clay particles are extremely fine (<0.002 mm) with strong electro-chemical inter-particle attraction, making clay a highly cohesive soil.

q: 4. At liquid limit a soil has .............
options: nothing to do with shear strength
explain: The liquid limit marks the water content at which soil has negligible shear strength, transitioning from plastic to liquid state.

q: 5. When the plastic limit cannot be determined, the soil is reported to be .............
explain: If the soil cannot be rolled into threads to determine plastic limit, it is classified as non-plastic.

q: 6. The specific gravity of sand is approximately
explain: Sand is composed mainly of quartz, whose specific gravity is close to 2.65, commonly rounded to about 2.6.

q: 7. A soil consisting of approximately equal percentage of sand, silt and clay is referred to as .............
explain: Loam is defined as soil with roughly equal proportions of sand, silt, and clay-sized particles.

q: 8. In the field, sand can be distinguished from silt by .............
explain: The dilatancy test shows a characteristic surface sheen reaction in sand and silty sand, helping distinguish sand from silt in the field.

q: 9. Shaking test is also called as .............
explain: The shaking test and dilatancy test refer to the same field identification procedure.

q: 10. The field, dilatancy test is used to differentiate clay from .............
explain: The dilatancy (shaking) test is primarily used to distinguish clay (no water reaction) from silts (which show a dilatant surface sheen).

q: 11. Maximum size of clay particle is
explain: By the standard grain-size classification, particles finer than 0.002 mm (2 microns) are classed as clay.

q: 12. The soil which contains finest grain particles, is
explain: Clay has the smallest particle size (<0.002 mm) among the options, making it the finest-grained soil.

q: 13. The basis for all soil classification systems is
explain: Engineering soil classification (like USCS or AASHTO) primarily relies on grain size distribution and Atterberg limits (plasticity).

q: 14. Hydrometer is a device which is used to measure .............
explain: A hydrometer measures the specific gravity (relative density) of a liquid or suspension.

q: 15. The range of values printed on a hydrometer are .............
explain: Standard soil hydrometers used in sedimentation analysis are calibrated over roughly 0.995 to 1.040.

q: 16. The basis for all soil classification system is .............
explain: Engineering soil classification systems (like USCS) are built on grain size distribution and plasticity characteristics.

q: 17. Silts have the following property
explain: Unlike clays, silts generally exhibit very little to no plasticity because they lack a significant plate-like mineral structure.

q: 18. The maximum size of clay particle is
explain: By standard definition, clay consists of particles with a diameter smaller than 0.002 mm (2 microns).

q: 19. The property of a soil which allows it to be deformed rapidly without rupture, elastic rebound and also a volume change, is known
explain: Plasticity is the property allowing rapid deformation without cracking, remoulding, and volume change, characteristic of fine-grained cohesive soils.

q: 20. For general engineering purposes, soils are classified by
explain: The Unified Soil Classification System (USCS) is the most widely adopted system for general civil/geotechnical engineering purposes worldwide.

q: 21. Soils containing organic matters
options: shrink with increase of moisture content
explain: Organic soils (peats etc.) have a fibrous, porous, spongy texture due to decomposed plant matter, giving low bearing capacity and high compressibility.

q: 22. Which of the following clay mineral gives maximum swelling?
explain: Montmorillonite has an expansive lattice structure, giving it the highest swelling potential among common clay minerals.

q: 23. Gravel and sand is a .............
explain: Gravel and sand are coarse-grained soils that lack cohesion between particles, making them non-cohesive coarse-grained soils.

q: 24. Stoke's law is used to determine the .............
options: grain size distribution of those soils whose grain size is finer than 0.075 mm
explain: Stoke's Law is applied in sedimentation (hydrometer) analysis to determine the grain size distribution of fine particles finer than 0.075 mm.

q: 25. When the hydrometer analysis is performed, it requires correction for .............
explain: Hydrometer readings must be corrected for temperature, meniscus, and dispersing agent effects — all three corrections apply.

q: 26. According to Stoke's law, the velocity at which grains settle out of suspension, all other factors being equal, is dependent upon .............
explain: Stoke's Law settling velocity depends on grain shape, weight (density), and size together.

q: 27. The smallest sieve size according to Indian standards is .............
explain: The finest standard IS sieve size used in grain size analysis is 0.045 mm.

q: 28. Sieving is not practicable for grain sizes smaller than about .............
explain: Below about 0.075 mm, particles are too fine for mechanical sieving and sedimentation (hydrometer) analysis is used instead.

q: 29. The shear strength in plastic untrained clay, is due to
explain: In saturated plastic (undrained) clay tested quickly, pore pressures prevent frictional resistance from developing, so shear strength is essentially due to cohesion alone (φ=0 condition).

q: 30. A soil having particles of nearly the same size is known as .............
explain: A uniform soil has particles concentrated in a narrow size range, giving a low uniformity coefficient.

q: 31. A soil having uniformity co-efficient more than 10, is called .............
explain: A high uniformity coefficient (Cu > 10) indicates a wide range of particle sizes, characteristic of a well graded soil.

q: 32. In hydrometer analysis the principle used is
explain: Stokes' Law governs the terminal velocity of spherical particles falling through a liquid, which is the basis for hydrometer tests.

q: 33. The property of the soil which permits it to be deformed rapidly without volume change, rupture and elastic rebound is termed as .............
explain: Plasticity is the property that allows soil to be remoulded/deformed without volume change, cracking, or elastic rebound.

q: 34. The liquidity index is given as .............
explain: Liquidity Index (LI) = (natural water content - plastic limit) / plasticity index.

q: 35. When other factors remaining constant, the velocity with which as soil grain settle out of suspension depends upon .............
explain: As per Stoke's Law, settling velocity depends jointly on the grain's shape, size, and weight.

q: 36. The angle of internal friction of clays, is usually
explain: Because of their platy, fine particles and high cohesion, clays typically show a low drained friction angle in the range of about 5° to 20°.

q: 37. The angle of internal friction is maximum for
explain: Angular grains interlock more, and dense packing increases interlocking further, so angular-grained dense sand gives the highest angle of internal friction.

q: 38. Particle size range is measured by
explain: The uniformity coefficient (Cu) provides a measure of the range of particle sizes present in a soil sample.

q: 39. Thixotropy of soils refers to .............
options: gain of strength of soil with passage of time after it has been remoulded
loss of strength of soil with passage of time after it had been remoulded
thickening of soil with particles with water
explain: Thixotropy is the phenomenon of a remoulded soil gradually regaining strength over time without any change in water content.

q: 40. The ratio of the compressive strength of unconfined clay in an undisturbed state to that in a remoulded state is .............
explain: This ratio defines sensitivity, which is always greater than one since remoulding reduces clay strength.

q: 41. The effective size of particle of soil is given by
explain: Effective size is defined as the diameter (D10) for which 10% of the soil particles are finer.

q: 42. D10 of soil is the diameter in mm such that
options: 10% of the soil is coarser than this value
10% of the soil is finer than this value
this value has no bearing on particle size distribution
explain: D10 represents the size at which 10 percent of the sample by weight consists of smaller particles.

q: 43. The compressibility of the following soil is somewhat less .............
explain: Among these organic/inorganic clays and silts of varying plasticity, OL (low plasticity organic clay) has comparatively lower compressibility.

q: 44. The coefficient of curvature is defined as
explain: Coefficient of curvature Cc = (D30)² / (D60 × D10), used along with Cu to assess gradation of a soil.

q: 45. The workability of the following soil is better .............
explain: Being lower plasticity, OL soil is comparatively easier to work with as a construction material than the higher-plasticity options.

q: 46. Soil in which some of the intermediate size particles are missing is known as .............
explain: A gradation curve missing some intermediate particle sizes (a gap-graded curve) defines a skip graded soil.

q: 47. The ratio of plasticity index to percentage of clay finer than 2 micron, is known as
explain: Activity number (A) measures the plasticity of the clay fraction; it is the ratio of the plasticity index to the percentage of clay-sized particles.

q: 48. Soil which contains the particles of different sizes in good proportion is called .............
explain: A well graded soil has a continuous, balanced distribution of particle sizes across a wide range.

q: 49. The ratio of plasticity index to flow index is called
explain: Toughness index (It) is defined as the ratio of the plasticity index to the flow index, indicating the shear strength of the soil at the plastic limit.

q: 50. In the hydrometer analysis, the effective depth will be .............
explain: As per the reference answer key, the effective depth of the hydrometer bulb is taken to increase as the test proceeds.
